title: Reviews held by people
now: SRR, PDR, CDR and QR exist in kyr rms only as records played by one operator driving ten scripted accounts (JRR); the review group of the SRevP has not met on this package.
closes_with: Each review held on the package regenerated at the reviewed commit: the participants log in as themselves and enter their own RIDs, dispositions and decision; at least one reviewer who did not author the reviewed items; the JRR then names them from the export.
who: The owner convenes; a named reviewer who is not the author; for QR, a consuming repository's maintainer.
rms_feature: Actors on every revision, approval and baseline (S-04); the review kernel (E-03).

title: Category, tailoring and coverage targets agreed with a counter-party
now: Category D, the tailoring (PAF/TAILORING.md) and the coverage targets 80 % / 65 % (UUID7-SRS-090) are the supplier's proposal; there is no customer and no requirements baseline, so the system-to-software traceability (E-40 5.8.3.2a) has no upper level.
closes_with: A reusing project agrees the category from its system analysis (Q-80 D.1), the tailoring (E-40 Annex S) and the coverage figures (E-40 5.8.3.5b), and approves them in the rms; a user-needs document stands for the RB so that the TS traces to an upper level.
who: A consuming project's owner acting as customer.
rms_feature: A customer role whose approval of the tailoring document and of UUID7-SRS-090 is recorded with its actor.

title: Acceptance review and certificate of conformance
now: UUID7-REV-AR is proposed and has no baseline; no customer has run acceptance; no certificate of conformance (Q-80 7.3.7) is issued.
closes_with: A consumer runs its acceptance (its pipeline with the released debs pinned) on the released configuration; the AR is held and its baseline frozen and approved by that consumer; the certificate of conformance is issued for that version.
who: A consuming repository's maintainer as customer; the owner as supplier.
rms_feature: A baseline that carries the release it accepts (commit, tag, deb SHA-256) (E-02, E-06).

title: Configuration identified by a release
now: The current version has no tag; the evidence's commit is on a work branch, not master; v1.1.2 is lightweight and v1.1.1 unsigned (SCMP); the rms baselines name no commit and freeze members at any status (SCF, configuration flags).
closes_with: Release the version through the shared cicd workflow from the pinned root: an annotated, signed tag on master; ecss/make.sh run from that tag (OI-10) so that the evidence carries the tag, the root identity and SHA256SUMS; SCF and SRelD regenerated from the released debs; every rms review baseline frozen with the commit it froze.
rms_feature: A baseline freeze that records the uuid7 commit and the artifacts' SHA-256 (kyr-rms-cli baseline has no option for either today), admits only approved members or lists the rest as not in the baseline, and is refused for QR/AR without them.

title: Actors recorded in the rms export
now: The committed export names no actor on any revision, approval or baseline; the first approval of a two-person approval leaves no record; ecss.py refuses such an export as the source of truth (RED).
closes_with: kyr_rms stores the acting person on every revision, records the first approval and its consumption as audit events, exports the approvers per revision and who froze and approved each baseline; the export is refreshed (rms_tests/export.sh) and ecss.py accepts it.
who: The owner (kyr_rms); whoever refreshes the export.
rms_feature: changed_by on every revision; approvals per revision; baseline created_by and approved_by in the package export (kyr_rms 0.38.0).

title: Tools without prior use and the rms version
now: ecss/tools/ecss.py was written for this package and kyr_rms is used as an ECSS source of truth for the first time, so neither meets the category D condition of Q-80 5.6.1.1 (prior successful use); the export does not carry the kyr_rms version that produced it; no customer agreed the tool list.
closes_with: A second project uses both tools successfully (or each is qualified as a tool by its own verification); the package export carries the kyr_rms version, which the SPAP's tool table then prints; a counter-party agrees the list (OI-02).
who: The owner (kyr_rms export field; a second user of ecss.py).
rms_feature: A kyr_rms_version field in the package export.

title: ECSS category and interfaces in the rms
now: The rms criticality field is a workflow priority (two approvers from high), not an ECSS category; the ECSS category lives in the applicability field by convention; the ICD items are imported as requirements, not interfaces.
closes_with: The rms carries the ECSS category per project and per item (or names its field priority), and the ICD rows are imported as interface artifacts; TAILORING <3.1> then maps one field to the other without convention.
rms_feature: An ecss_category field per project and per item; interface as an import kind.

title: Technical budgets as requirements and rms results
now: Timing (UUID7-SRS-040) and static memory (UUID7-SRS-050, -051) have budgets and are measured; stack and code size are measured at every refresh (SVR <5>) without a budget; no budget is recorded as an rms result at a review; no customer specified them.
closes_with: Budget requirements for stack and code size with their margins in the rms; each budget recorded as a result at CDR and QR; the margin philosophy agreed with a counter-party (OI-02).
who: The owner (requirements); the reviewers at CDR and QR.
rms_feature: None beyond results on budget requirements.
